articles.title: Delhi traffic police issues advisory for Kashmere Gate ahead of protest at Chief Electoral officer’s office on October 7 - Business Upturn
articles.full_text:
Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory warning commuters that traffic movement in and around Kashmere Gate is likely to be affected on October 7 from 12:00 noon to 3:30 pm, in view of a proposed protest or demonstration at the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi. The advisory, posted on X, urged commuters to avoid affected stretches, plan their journeys in advance, use alternate routes and follow the directions of Delhi Traffic Police personnel.
“Motorists are requested to remain patient, follow traffic rules and cooperate with traffic personnel deployed in the area. Please follow diversion signs and traffic directions to avoid congestion,” the advisory stated. The protest is part of the INDIA bloc’s ongoing campaign over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and its demand for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The advisory comes a day after the INDIA bloc’s march from Parliament to the Election Commission headquarters on October 6, which saw traffic restrictions imposed across parts of central Delhi, including Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, Parliament Street, Ashoka Road and Jantar Mantar Road. The Delhi Traffic Police had then advised commuters to avoid unnecessary travel through affected areas, expect diversions and barricading, and prefer Metro or public transport wherever feasible.
The protest at the Chief Electoral Officer’s office in Kashmere Gate is part of the bloc’s district-level protests announced for October 7 and 8, with a mass demonstration also planned at the same office on November 7. Delhi Metro has shut entry and exit at 12 stations due to the protests, with commuters travelling between Kashmere Gate and Central Secretariat advised to use the Violet Line.
